module_title: DPSP - Constitutional Amendments, FR Conflicts, and Landmark Judgments
introduction: This advanced level provides a critical analysis of new DPSPs added via amendments, the historical legal tussle between Fundamental Rights (FRs) and DPSPs (from Champakam Dorairajan to Minerva Mills), and their actual utility in jurisprudence.

core_concepts.title: DPSPs added by the 42nd Amendment (1976)
core_concepts.description: Indira Gandhi's government added 4 new principles: Art 39A (Equal justice and free legal aid), Art 39(f) (Healthy development of children), Art 43A (Participation of workers in management of industries), and Art 48A (Protection of environment, forests, and wildlife).

core_concepts.title: DPSPs added by other Amendments
core_concepts.description: 44th Amendment (1978): Added Art 38(2) (Minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities). 97th Amendment (2011): Added Art 43B (Promotion of Co-operative Societies).

core_concepts.title: FR vs. DPSP: The Historic Tussle
core_concepts.description: In the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951), the SC ruled that FRs are superior. In the Golaknath case (1967), it said FRs cannot be amended for implementing DPSPs. Parliament retaliated by passing the 25th Amendment Act (1971).

core_concepts.title: Impact of Article 31C (The Exception)
core_concepts.description: The 25th Amendment inserted Art 31C, which states that if the State makes a law to implement the socialistic DPSPs in Art 39(b) and 39(c), it cannot be declared void on the ground that it violates the Fundamental Rights under Article 14 (Equality) or Article 19 (Freedoms).

core_concepts.title: Minerva Mills Case (1980)
core_concepts.description: In this landmark judgment, the Supreme Court struck down the absolute primacy of DPSP over FRs and held that the Indian Constitution is founded on the 'bedrock of balance' between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles. Neither is absolutely supreme over the other.

important_entities.name: K.C. Wheare
important_entities.significance: He critically called the Directive Principles a 'manifesto of aims and aspirations' and a 'dustbin of sentiments'.

important_entities.name: Sir B.N. Rau
important_entities.significance: He recommended to the Constituent Assembly that individual rights should be divided into two categories: Justiciable (Fundamental Rights) and Non-justiciable (DPSP).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: As a general rule, Fundamental Rights are supreme. But as a strict 'exception' under Article 31C, laws implementing Article 39(b) and 39(c) (equitable distribution of wealth) have override power over Articles 14 and 19.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) largely added new directive principles by appending a capital 'A' to existing articles.

exam_strategy_tips: Identifying 'Which of the following DPSP was NOT in the original constitution?' (i.e., added by the 42nd or 44th Amendment) is a recurring question in UPSC and State PCS.
In Assertion-Reasoning questions, deeply understand the 'Harmonious Construction' (balance theory) established in the Minerva Mills Case.
